chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever says, when entering the evening, three times:
'Glory be to God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, at nightfall and at midday' (Quran 30:17-18)

no good occurring that night will miss him, and all its evil will be repelled from him. And whoever says the same when entering the morning, no good occurring that day will miss him, and all its evil will be repelled from him.

key_terms.صرف عنه شره: Its evil is repelled from him — divine protection through Quranic recitation
key_terms.فسبحان الله: Glory be to God — the opening word of the Quranic verse being recited, an expression of divine transcendence
key_terms.لم يفته خير: No goodness will escape/miss him — a guarantee of spiritual benefit for the reciter

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verse did Imam Ali recommend reciting morning and evening for protection?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) teaches that reciting Quran 30:17-18 three times at the start of evening and morning provides spiritual protection: it guarantees attainment of all goodness of that period and repels all its evil. This narration is transmitted through a long chain of reliable Shia narrators from al-Saduq's Amali assemblies. The original audience would have understood this as a prophylactic dhikr — a practice of divine remembrance that creates a spiritual shield around the one who performs it faithfully.
